[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-1om[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Make machine capacity legible and correct[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]The header capacity chip always matches what runner admission sees [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]on this machine, and every unit (or zero) can be traced to a named [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]agent and a stated reason: on the chip, on every Running-bucket [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]row, in a keyboard-reachable inspector, and from `sase agent load`.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]The athena screenshot case (6 running, 5.0 occupied) reads `5/8`, [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]not `3/8`.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]9[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]5[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]

[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Stop the TUI roster from dropping monitors and mislabelling [/bold #D7AFFF]  [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]holders[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]roster-fixes[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]roster-fixes: give monitor rows their supervisor PID from agent_meta [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF](then the running marker) on every loader path, index holders by agent [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]row instead of workflow-step rows (closing task bead sase-1ol), and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]carry runner_claim_owner_key through the roster projection, with [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]loader-level regression tests.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Per-record capacity accounting in the Rust snapshot[/bold #D7AFFF]           [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]core-accounting[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]core-accounting: in sase-core, add an accounting list (state, charged [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]weight, weight source, claim, reason code) covering every request [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]record, a top-level validity flag, and a monitor-inherited weight input;[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]bump the schema version, update the binding, and adapt sase's record [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]builders and legacy fallback.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Shared authoritative machine capacity report[/bold #D7AFFF]                  [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]machine-report[dim] · [dim][/dim]after core-accounting[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]machine-report: one read-only Python adapter that builds the machine's [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]capacity report from admission's shared scan cache, a fresh liveness [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]probe, active holds, and the Rust snapshot, plus limit provenance, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]machine label, age, and a bounded rescan policy.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]The sase agent load command and shared capacity view model[/bold #D7AFFF]    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]load-cli[dim] · [dim][/dim]after machine-report[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]load-cli: a TUI-free view model (holders, live rows holding nothing [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]grouped by reason, queued rows with real blockers, diagnostics) rendered[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]by a new `sase agent load [-j]` command, plus a Reference section [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]listing what holds capacity.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Retire the Python holder predicate behind sase agent list[/bold #D7AFFF]     [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
    [#AF87FF]list-holder-parity[dim] · [dim][/dim]after machine-report[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]list-holder-parity: source `holds_runner_slot`, `runner_slot_holders`, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and `runner_slots_in_use` in `sase agent list -j` from Rust accounting, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]delete `runner_slot_holder_dirs` and the `status == "RUNNING"` fallback,[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and add per-entry capacity fields.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Feed the TUI from the authoritative report[/bold #D7AFFF]                    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]tui-report-feed[dim] · [dim][/dim]after roster-fixes, machine-report[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]tui-report-feed: compute the machine report off the event loop on token [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]change plus a 10 s poll, drive the chip values and row queue context [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]from it, keep the roster projection only as a pre-first-report estimate [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and drift witness, and log capacity_gauge/capacity_drift telemetry.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  7 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Machine-labelled cap chip with provenance, staleness, fault, [/bold #D7AFFF] [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]and overage[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]cap-chip[dim] · [dim][/dim]after tui-report-feed[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]cap-chip: rename the gauge to a machine-labelled `cap` chip that keeps [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]its label in compact density, marks overrides, staleness, invalid [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]accounting, and over-limit load, teaches running-versus-cap in the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]tooltip and `?` help, and fixes the misleading docs example.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  8 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Occupancy marks on Running rows and a Capacity detail line[/bold #D7AFFF]    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]occupancy-marks[dim] · [dim][/dim]after tui-report-feed[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]occupancy-marks: attach accounting entries to Agent rows, draw a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]charged-now mark on every Running-bucket agent node and clan container [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF](including collapsed clans), and add a never-suppressed `Capacity:` line[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]to agent and clan detail cards.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  9 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Keyboard-first capacity inspector[/bold #D7AFFF]                             [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]capacity-inspector[dim] · [dim][/dim]after load-cli, cap-chip[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]capacity-inspector: a modal rendering the shared view model, opened from[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]a chip click, leader `,l`, and the command palette, with jump-to-agent [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]rows, complete or explicitly truncated lists, real queue blockers, and a[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]copy-snapshot action.[/#D7D7AF]
